Resolves #18318
Related: #18304

`Workspace` is a façade, and until now nothing said what that meant. Every extraction in this Epic had to infer which callbacks the host still owed its collaborators, and an inferred façade becomes a forwarding shell one method at a time. This states the contract, guards the one rule that had a price tag and no enforcement, and records the Ownership-test verdict for the file as a whole.

This is the last open leaf of #18304.

Evidence: L1 (documentation) + L2 (two unit arms, both red-first against real violations) → L1/L2 required. Residual: AC-4, Residual-Owner: #18314 — **accepted** by its owner at [issuecomment-5559432526](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18318#issuecomment-5559432526), applied to this leaf directly and to the #18314 body.

## Ownership test (AC-5)

Measured with one instrument across both refs, which is the valid comparison:

| | `131c782ca8` | HEAD | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| methods | 105 | 79 | **−26** |
| getters | 2 | 2 | 0 |
| config + class-state declarations | 50 | 36 | **−14** |
| code lines | 1742 | 1214 | **−528** |
| total lines | 4319 | 3288 | **−1031** |

1. **Did `Workspace` lose the methods, configs and mutable state?** Yes, across the Epic: 26 methods and 14 declarations gone, no forwarding wrappers (AC-7).
2. **Can each extracted owner be instantiated and destroyed independently under a bounded interface?** Yes — `plugin/Maximize`, `projection/HeaderActionPolicy`, and `window/TearOut`'s seam bundle each construct and retire on their own; the last is driven end-to-end with no browser and no component.
3. **Can a consumer replace or disable one without overriding a dozen `Workspace` methods?** Yes. `apps/workstation` overrides three generic methods where it previously reimplemented four tear-out-named ones.
4. **Did cross-concern calls fall, or become `owner.foo()` wrappers?** Fell: `tearOut*` references in `dock/Workspace.mjs` 226 → 169, with zero retired names surviving anywhere.

**Verdict: PASS, with AC-4's consumer-side consolidation carried by #18314.** The façade owns ordering and the one mutation boundary; it owns no concern outright.

## Deltas from ticket

**The baseline's own figures do not fully reproduce, so I report deltas rather than adopt absolutes.** The ticket quotes `1,742` code lines and `50` declarations at `131c782ca8` — both reproduce **exactly**. It also quotes `4,255` total and `110` methods, which reproduce with neither `wc -l` (4318) nor an AST count (105) at that ref. I do not know which instrument produced those two, so every figure above is measured with one instrument across both refs; the deltas are valid regardless of the absolute.

**Correction to this PR's first version: I called the ticket's `read`/`prepare`/`adopt`/`project` naming "aspirational". It is not.** It names the **generic participant protocol** the transaction manager executes, which is enforced rather than documented — a participant missing `capture`/`prepare`/`adopt`/`compensate` has its transaction refused, `capture` throws unless it returns `{value, generation, revision}` synchronously, and `adopt`/`compensate` are synchronous by requirement because a compensation that could await is a window in which a half-adopted topology is observable. I had been reading only the dock adapter's callback list and mistook one layer for the whole thing. Both are now stated, and `project` is corrected to take the transaction **context** — the committed value is read from `context.snapshot`, and the adapter adds `preserveItemIds` naming panes owned by sibling participants.

**AC-2's rule needed a sharper instrument than the ticket implies.** `manager.Transaction` IS reachable from the dock — through a **dynamic** import, which is the lazy boundary the Group work landed deliberately. So the arm measures the STATIC closure and separately asserts the dynamic edge still exists: a grep for the module name reports the intended design as a violation, and a rule that fires on its own feature gets suppressed within a week.

**An encode/decode round-trip guard was added and then removed.** The integration branch resolves vessel ownership by matching the exact reserved workspace key and has already deleted the base decoder — verified: zero references there, against three on `dev`. The hazard the guard pinned exists only because ownership is recovered by DECODING a key, so the successor retires it by construction. I first attached a sunset note asking its owner to delete it; that is avoidable merge work, and a retirement comment is not a substitute for not adding the thing. Removed.

**AC-7's five surviving delegations, each with its reason:** `applyDockZoneOperation` (the sanctioned reducer entry the Neural Link dock-holder contract resolves against), `onDockPaneReturn` (an overridable observation hook), `createProjectionPlaceholder` (a factory), and `resolveRevealPane` / `resolveFreshPane` (documented defaults that delegate to `resolvePane`, each stating why a consumer would override). None proxies a retired API.

## Test Evidence

All coverage runs in CI. The two arms are red-first against real violations rather than against their own predicates:

- **import direction** — adding a real `import` of the topology manager to `dock/Workspace.mjs` reds DIRECTION A **alone** and names both crossings (`Transaction.mjs` and, transitively, `transaction/Commit.mjs`), which is also the evidence the walk recurses rather than matching direct imports. Two anti-vacuity guards, because an empty closure would pass both directions for free: each closure must be substantial and must reach `core/Base.mjs` several hops down. A fourth arm asserts the manager stays reachable **lazily** — without it, DIRECTION A would still pass on the day the feature it protects disappeared.
- **import-free crossing** — `window/TearOut.mjs` has a static closure of exactly **one module: itself**, so no transitive walk can ever surface it through another module. Direction B's first predicate named `Workspace` and `WorkspaceDocument` only and caught **0** of it; the rule is now the dock directory and a dedicated control pins that case. The innocent-neighbour list no longer contains a dock module — it previously asserted one was innocent under the manager rule, encoding the exemption the rule exists to forbid.

`unit 3416/3416`.
